alternatives.argument: Definition is supplied locally: the published p-FEM Hilbert convention is extended to a stated real Banach triple with explicit canonical map and weak derivative tests.

The local proof covers arbitrary bounded open sets: d=1 uses zero extension, the fundamental theorem, Holder and Arzela-Ascoli, while d>=2 uses a valid subcritical exponent reduction. It proves continuity and density on both branches.
The local proof derives Bochner translations from simple-function approximation and scalar Lp translation continuity, then proves mollifier and variable-cell-average convergence.
The local proof establishes interior energy identities by time mollification, Cauchy convergence in C(K;H), and endpoint strong traces by the averaged energy estimate.
The local proof constructs finite-dimensional H projections from compactness, bounds scalar coefficients by their Lq derivatives, and completes the total-boundedness and Lr-upgrade arguments.
The local proof compares piecewise-constant and affine reconstructions, bounds their defect and translates, and carries out the finite-dimensional coefficient compactness argument.

The local proof identifies the Bochner gradient as a closed range, explicitly supplies its simple-function product-space isometry by Tonelli, extracts a weak limit under the stated Choice dependencies, and identifies the strong H limit on every bounded open domain.

The local proof supplies the nonlinear time-step existence and energy bounds, compact state convergence, weak flux extraction, endpoint lower semicontinuity, and Minty identification; its explicit interval and cube cases use the separately proved projector carrier.
The local proof subtracts the two equations, uses the chain rule, and proves the explicit scaled Young estimate under the stated strong-monotonicity hypothesis.

sources.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024
sources.locator: The complete 43-page PDF was fetched and read. Relevant material: §0 Minty trick; Theorem 2.1 Galerkin/Brouwer; §4 p-Laplacian; Theorem 8.8 and Corollary 8.9.1; §9 evolution problems.

contents.name: Minty trick for a monotone flux
contents.support: The notes present the Minty perturbation route. The local proof expands the weak pairings, supplies the limsup condition, and completes the dominated-convergence argument.

contents.name: Finite-dimensional Galerkin existence by Brouwer
contents.support: The notes use an outward-pointing finite-dimensional map. The local item derives the time-step map, its coercive sphere bound, and the uniform discrete energy and derivative estimates.

contents.name: p-Laplacian flux and p-growth hypotheses
contents.support: The notes identify the p-Laplacian as a standard monotone flux. The example independently proves monotonicity, growth, coercivity, and Nemytskii continuity.

contents.name: Aubin–Lions and evolution equation framework
contents.support: The notes give the compactness and evolution framework. The carrier proves the exact conforming discrete scheme and Minty limsup argument with its projector interface.

contents.name: Minty–Browder monotonicity identification

contents.name: L2 projection locality and graph-distance decay
contents.support: The paper establishes a graph-locality and graph-distance decay route for L2 projection. This carrier independently proves entrywise inverse decay by a Neumann series using its uniform spectral bound and polynomial graph-ball count, and also proves the uniform row and column sums needed by the Lr argument.

contents.support: The paper supports the Lp stability, inverse estimate, approximation-operator proof route. Its mesh assumptions differ; the local carrier supplies the exact globally quasi-uniform simplex and directly defined interval cases with complete proofs.
